# Sirach Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 1

---

1 All wisdom comes from the Lord, and with him it endures forever.

2 The sands of the sea, the drops of rain, the days of eternity — who can count them?

3 The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, the depths of the abyss — who can search them out?

4 Wisdom was created before all other things, and prudent understanding from the very beginning.

5 The source of wisdom is the word of God on high, and her paths are the everlasting commandments.

6 To whom has the root of wisdom been disclosed? Who has understood her subtle workings?

7 To whom has the knowledge of wisdom been revealed? Who has grasped the abundance of her experience?

8 There is one who is wise — greatly to be feared, seated on his throne: the Lord.

9 He himself created her, saw her, measured her, and poured her out upon all his works.

10 She is present among all people according to his bounty, and he lavished her upon those who love him.

11 The fear of the Lord is honor and glory, gladness and a festive crown of joy.

12 The fear of the Lord gladdens the heart, bringing happiness and joy and long life.

13 For those who fear the Lord, all will go well at the last; on the day of their death they will be blessed.

14 To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; she was woven into those who are faithful from their birth.

15 Among human beings she has built her home as an eternal foundation; among their descendants she will be trusted.

16 To be filled with the fear of the Lord is true wisdom; she makes those who hold her drink from the fruit of her deeds.

17 She fills their whole house with choice things, and their storehouses with her produce.

18 The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, causing peace and full health to flourish.

19 He rained down knowledge and discerning understanding, and glorified those who cling to her.

20 The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord; long life grows from her branches.

21 The fear of the Lord drives away sins; where it is present, it turns back wrath.

22 A hot-tempered person has no justification — his very anger will prove his ruin.

23 A patient person will endure until the right moment, and afterward joy will burst forth for him.

24 Until the proper time he will hold his words back, and the lips of many will proclaim his understanding.

25 In the treasury of wisdom are proverbs of instruction; but to a sinner, worship of God is an abomination.

26 If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will grant her to you freely.

27 For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction; loyalty and humility are his delight.

28 Do not defy the fear of the Lord; do not approach him with a divided heart.

29 Do not play the hypocrite before others; guard what comes from your lips.

30 Do not exalt yourself lest you fall and bring dishonor upon yourself. The Lord will expose your secrets and cast you down in the midst of the assembly, because you did not truly come near to the fear of the Lord, and your heart was full of deceit.

---

## Council Notes

**On "fear of the Lord" (phobos kyriou):** All three agents rendered this consistently. SOPHIA retains "fear" throughout — this is Ben Sira's central concept and should not be softened to "reverence" or "awe," though those are accurate. The term encompasses both awe and moral accountability.

**On v.4 vs. v.14 "beginning of wisdom":** Vaticanus reads v.14 as "the root of wisdom is to fear the Lord" and v.4 focuses on wisdom's pre-creation priority. SOPHIA inserts "beginning" at v.14 following the Hebrew fragment tradition which has "reshit chokmah yir'at Adonai" (Prov 9:10 parallel).

**On v.5 and v.7:** These verses are textually uncertain (absent from some manuscripts). Included here because Vaticanus contains them. EMET's footnote is noted.

**Verse count:** 30 verses (some numbering systems vary; Vaticanus tradition followed).
